text.text_excerpt: Dinner Lab met all my expectations...I really loved the unusual cuisine (North Korean this week) and the staff was amazing. Water bottles on the table so you could help yourself. Free pouring wine and a pseudo-mojito made with a Korean liquor. Awesome! And then five courses of yummy food and the servers remembered that I was a problem child who received off menu needs. (Yes, I'm special.) I will say that your dinner companions can really make these events. The person to my right kept his back to me all night as he leaned into his large group so that was odd. But our dinner companions across from us (the seating was huge long banquet style) were lovely and we had a great time chatting with...

My SO and I finally got to our second Dinner Lab last night. And we invited our moms! It was a brunch at "Castillo Blanco," which serves as the Den for the Krewe of Chewbacchus. The venue was... interesting. Lots of off props and laser lights. And somewhat loud music. Anyway, we were excited for our brunch. The chef was Tan Uckan, who is originally from Turkey. And he is the chef de cuisine at Stanley, which is a top-notch brunch place in the French Quarter. Now, on to the meal... Amuse: rice and barley pudding with almonds, walnuts, and dried fruits. The pudding itself had the consistency of oatmeal, and my serving did not have as much fruit as I would've liked. Still pretty good though....

I have only been to one event, but it was outstanding! Trisha does a good job at coordinating these events with local empty and interesting spaces in town. The chefs were from Austin when I went this past Sunday 11/10/13. The cost of the event was $50, which included 5 courses and unlimited beverages. You are sat at large tables with groups of people, which is fun in itself to network. I went with my sister and we had a great time. The service was outstanding, especially considering these people are not working for tips (we tipped anyway). I assume they are being compensated pretty well, however. It is definitely a fun and interesting concept. This would be a great 1st(or 2nd and 3rd) dat...
